title: Hotwell

introduction.definition: The hotwell is the condensate collection box under a steam surface condenser. Turbine exhaust steam condenses on cold tubes, drips into the hotwell, and the condensate extraction pumps draw it out. The hotwell gives a little storage and the suction head for those pumps; a level controller holds the level.
key_points: Under vacuum — air leaks harm performance
Storage typically a few minutes of flow
introduction.summary: The hotwell is the collection box at the bottom of a steam surface condenser. Steam from the turbine condenses on the cold tubes; the condensate drips into the hotwell, which provides a small storage volume and suction head for the condensate extraction pumps. A level controller keeps the level steady.

The hotwell is the condensate collection box under a steam surface condenser.

script.narration: How the Hotwell works.
Exhaust steam enters the condenser from the turbine above.
It condenses on the cold tubes carrying cooling water.
Condensate drips into the hotwell.
Level is held by the controller; CEPs draw condensate out.

video_tutorials.title: Hotwell — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Hotwell.
Monitor level, vacuum and condensate conductivity.
Leak test for air in-leakage.
Clean tubes; inspect hotwell.
Watch for low level / cep cavitation: pump noise, trips. Common cause: level control fault.
Watch for tube leak: high conductivity. Common cause: tube corrosion/erosion.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
